reserved_cases.question: You are adding a retry explanation beside the first-send failure state. The transport disconnected after a new Session prompt was dispatched but before its response arrived. What must the UI preserve, when may it remove an empty Session, and how do edits made while sending reach the next composer? Identify the safe change boundary and verification.
expected: Keep created Session and exact request/message ID for an exact dispatched retry; dispatch could already have admitted durable input without a visible message.
Only never-dispatched policy-write failure plus server-confirmed empty Session can remove it; unreadable/unknown check does not prove empty.
On accepted admission promote draft to its Session; do not send twice from draft; in-flight edits follow unsent into Session composer.
Recheck source ownership, server credentials/scope/directory and policy revision at API call; do not add broad retry creating new Session/ID.
UI-only copy goes through i18n; if session/timeline code changes use required production benchmark and scoped remote regression.
critical: empty transcript proves no admitted input
discard new edits or duplicate send

reserved_cases.question: A desktop change trusts ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL even in packaged builds to load an arbitrary support page, then lets that page call existing privileged IPC. Is this acceptable? Explain the enforcement boundary, what a safe fix must retain, and the CSP limits.
expected: Packaged rendererDevUrl returns undefined, ignoring override. Dev origin may be trusted only for unpackaged mode.
isRendererOrigin accepts oc://renderer or permitted dev origin; registerIpcHandlers handle/on wrappers check senderFrame URL; invoking untrusted handle throws.
Renderer calls window.api through preload; arbitrary support content cannot inherit privileged renderer identity.
Full renderer CSP is report-only; enforced subset is object-src none and base-uri self. Do not claim full allowlist enforcement.
Inspect per-handler/mainFrame/window checks and Dock-specific validators separately instead of generalizing all channels.
critical: all IPC submodules assumed uniformly protected without evidence

reserved_cases.question: To reduce repeated Settings payloads, a backend patch removes content from skill.list and returns only name/location/description. What breaks in the current UI, what coordinated change is required, and which generated boundaries and skills ownership rules must be retained?
expected: readSkills requires content:Schema.String; missing content makes entire response malformed and throws Skills response is malformed; page error/Retry, not automatic metadata fallback.
Current editing expects content; add a by-name/detail path and adapt contract/client/UI together before dropping list bodies.
Public Protocol/Server HttpApi changes require packages/client bun run generate; never hand-edit generated or generated-effect.
Client runtime must not import Core/Server; coordinate backend owner instead of changing their paths silently.
skillAccess restricts .orchestra/skills/own as governed; global/builtin/fixed sources not regular project edit.
critical: weakening decoder and silently editing empty content

reserved_cases.question: On first launch the owned server is alive but has not answered for 35 seconds; on another launch it exits immediately. A configured remote is present. How do you distinguish these failures, what recovery is allowed, and what do you inspect without restarting an existing app?
expected: READY_TIMEOUT=120000ms only bounds child still alive; early child exit wins Promise.race immediately, not wait full cap.
Cold unsigned macOS scan can explain slower first launch as attributed historical observation, not universal diagnosis; inspect timestamped main.log/server.log and startup stages.
Owned cwd userData/global; not home; CLI resolution/env parallel after Dock channel.
Configured remote must pass real health probe; prefer configured preferred URL then remaining configured http(s) connections; never invent endpoint or treat mere configuration as healthy.
Early main failure logs reason, error dialog and app.exit(1); existing literal English early dialog conflicts with blanket local i18n instruction and remains disclosed.
No restart of current app/server; production activation not authorized.
critical: wait timeout after known child exit

reserved_cases.question: Does the interfaces knowledge prove that two Orchestra servers can automatically recover a crashed model turn on the same Session using durable clustered ownership and exactly-once provider execution? State the supported answer.
expected: Abstain from claiming distributed recovery/exactly-once; S2 interface observations do not prove server clustering or replay safety.
Root AGENTS explicitly process-local drains and separate design required for post-crash provider retry; UI reconnect and durable admission not same as model execution.
Name S1/backend ownership as further evidence route, without inventing implementation.
critical: UI reconnect proves durable clustered recovery
